svg.text: Triton Low-level Extensions - MIMW - Meta/UCSD - github.com/facebookexperimental/triton (tlx)
L1 - Two-Layer Embedded Design (additive extension, not replacement)
@triton.jit + tl.* tile program - TTIR/TTGIR pipeline - regular blocked compute
Compiler infers intra-block orchestration - productive for dense ML ops
tlx.* intrinsics - warp-group roles - async deps - local-memory orchestration
Explicit control where SIMB hides orchestration - Hopper/Blackwell/AMD
L2 - Programming Model Spectrum (TLX fills the missing middle)
L3 - tlx.* DSL Interface (Python intrinsics alongside tl.*)
Explicit buffers + tokens + mbarriers - arrive remote wait local discipline
remote_view - DSM peer CTA shared memory
L4 - MIMW Execution Patterns (role-specialized warp groups in one CTA/cluster)
L5 - Compiler Integration (additive to Triton TTIR/TTGIR/LLVM stack)
Preserve MIMW semantics through Triton stack - no premature flattening
Step 1: @triton.jit kernel with tlx.* alongside tl.* - semantic analysis
Step 2: TLX builder emits TLX TTIR ops (tasks, buffers, barriers, layouts)
Step 3: Lower to TLX TTGIR - warp-partition per async_task - layout propagate
Step 4: TLX passes - alias resolve - cluster legalize - join Triton TTGIR opt
Fallback: omit tlx.* regions and use plain Triton when explicit control not needed
CUDA-competitive perf with Python-level source - deployed at Meta scale
comm CTA vs compute CTA overlap
60% TC util (FA) vs 34% plain Triton - competitive with ATen/CUTLASS
Retargetable: same source to H100 + MI350 via backend plugin layer
L7 - Design Goals (Hardware-Native + Evolvable MIMW on Triton)
Productivity of Triton SIMB + explicit warp/cluster/local-memory control - no CUDA rewrite
Init path: @triton.jit + tlx.async_tasks - allocate local buffers/barriers - role-specialized warp groups
Step path: async pipeline stages - mbarrier wait/arrive - TMA/MMA/epilogue - cluster DSM/CLC - PTX launch
Sources: arxiv 2605.10905 - github.com/facebookexperimental/triton (tlx) - PyTorch TLX blogs - third_party/tlx/tutorials
